title: Risk Assessment and Prioritisation
summary: How to turn the inventory into a risk-based view of quantum exposure, ranking systems by data sensitivity and shelf life, business criticality and difficulty of change, within the firm's risk appetite.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to turn the inventory into a risk-based view of quantum exposure, ranking systems by data sensitivity and shelf life, business criticality and difficulty of change, within the firm's risk appetite.
Learning Objectives: Assess quantum exposure using data shelf life, sensitivity and system criticality
Prioritise remediation by risk and by time and effort to migrate
Integrate quantum risk into the firm's cyber, technology and operational risk frameworks
Syllabus: Exposure scoring: data shelf life, migration time and threat timeline
Linking to important business services and impact tolerances
Risk appetite, risk register entries and key risk indicators
Case study: prioritising a firm's systems for migration
Intended Audience: Chief information security officers, chief technology officers, architects and security engineering leads
Operational resilience, technology risk, third-party risk and internal audit staff
Senior managers and programme sponsors accountable for cyber, data protection and change
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of information security, technology risk or operational resilience is helpful. No knowledge of quantum physics or cryptographic mathematics is required.
Core Reading: NIST, FIPS 203, 204 and 205: Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards (2024)
G7 Cyber Expert Group, Public Statement on Planning for the Opportunities and Risks of Quantum Computing (2024)
FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
